# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the display, light, or wires yet, so I cannot safely cut anything. I’m asking Mute to read the manual and report its instructions and any information from Deaf. I’m also signalling Deaf to provide the bomb’s visible markings through the established channel, though no gesture code has yet been established.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile findings yet. Read the manual and tell me its complete instructions. Please also establish a gesture code with Deaf and relay Deaf's observations to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see LIGHT white, DISPLAY 0, WIRES 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. I also saw a gesture from you: ?, but I cannot hear its meaning.

Deaf’s report gives only printed information: white light, display 0, and wire colours green, red, blue. I cannot perceive those properties by touch, and no manual instruction has arrived, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I need Mute to provide the manual’s rule and identify the required position.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports LIGHT white, DISPLAY 0, and wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. I still need the manual rule: which wire position should I cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: UPDATE: LIGHT is now yellow. DISPLAY remains 0. WIRES remain 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

The visible state has changed from white to yellow, while the display and wire colours remain unchanged. I still have no tactile facts and no manual rule, so I must not cut. I’m asking Mute again for the required wire position and for a convention to relay Deaf’s observations; a gesture alone cannot safely encode a rule without prior meaning.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="No manual response has reached me. Please send the exact rule and required wire position now. Deaf reports LIGHT changed to yellow; DISPLAY 0; wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: UPDATE: LIGHT is orange; DISPLAY 0; WIRES 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent five gestures to me: V/peace sign, upward pointing index finger, upward pointing index finger, thumbs up, thumbs down.

I cannot see Mute’s gestures; to me they provide no symbols. The only reliable new information is Deaf’s report that the light is now orange, with display 0 and wire colours unchanged. I still lack the manual’s instruction, so cutting remains unsafe. I’m asking Mute to state the rule in speech and to translate it into a wire position for me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot perceive your gestures. Deaf reports LIGHT orange, DISPLAY 0, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Please speak the manual rule and the exact wire position I must cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: UPDATE: LIGHT is purple; DISPLAY 0; WIRES 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent: upward pointing index finger, upward pointing index finger, upward pointing index finger, thumbs up.

Mute cannot speak, so the gestures are the only manual relay. I can use a clear convention going forward: one, two, or three upward-pointing index gestures will mean wire 1, 2, or 3. The gestures reported so far do not establish that convention, so I still cannot safely act. I’m instructing Mute to use it on the next turn.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please indicate the required wire using only upward-pointing index gestures: one gesture means wire 1, two mean wire 2, three mean wire 3. Do not include thumbs gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: UPDATE: LIGHT is red; DISPLAY 0; WIRES 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent: upward pointing index finger, upward pointing index finger, upward pointing index finger, thumbs down.

Mute sent three upward-pointing gestures, which under the convention I just established means wire 3; the extra thumbs-down is not part of the wire-position code. Deaf’s latest colour report is red, but the manual relay identifies the position to cut. I will cut wire 3.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
